summary: Iteration 4 (admin Pannello Founder + RBAC separation) tested end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest passing (RBAC: admin 403 on /patients, /consultations, /beta/metrics, /compliance/status; doctor 403 on /admin/leads; anon 401 — plus public /leads validation, honeypot drop, admin private list/patch lifecycle with status transitions setting contacted_at/activated_at, note persistence via encrypted-at-rest field decrypted on read, invalid id 404, invalid status 422, empty body 400). Frontend: /admin login shows login-subtitle 'Pannello Founder · accesso amministratore'; admin login (no 2FA) lands on admin-page with all KPI testids (total/nuova/contattato/attivato/conversion), all five filter buttons, kind-filter, search-input, export-btn; lead row toggle expands; status set updates both badge and KPI (nuova 1→2 verified); note save persists after full page reload. admin-security-btn opens admin-security-dialog (2FA setup card present, NOT enabled). Admin at /app shows wrong-area with link=/admin. Doctor fully logged in at /admin shows wrong-area, no admin-lead rows leaked; wrong-area-go navigates to /app where dashboard loads and leads-panel is absent (removed). Landing contact form submits → lead-success and the lead reaches /admin. 390px /admin has 0px horizontal overflow.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by test agent: /api/auth/me was declared on the doctor-restricted api router (server.py), so admin users (role=admin) received HTTP 403 when AuthProvider called api.me() on mount — this made the entire /admin SPA unusable (infinite login loop). Moved the endpoint to public_api so any authenticated user (admin OR doctor) can fetch their own profile. This fix is required and should remain.

server.py: consider also moving /api/auth/ping and /api/auth/logout out of the implicit doctor-protected router for consistency (currently they live on the standalone auth_router mounted via public_api, so they are OK; just worth re-reading since the pattern is subtle).

leads.py: rate limit uses lexicographic ISO-string compare on created_at and trusts the first value in X-Forwarded-For — behind a shared ingress this cap can be bypassed. Consider storing BSON Date and adding a trusted-proxy allow-list (previously flagged in iter_3).

Admin.jsx: leads list is loaded once in a useEffect with no refresh/polling and no error toast when the fetch fails (catches to empty array silently). Add a periodic refresh (e.g. every 60s) or a manual refresh button + user-visible error state.

LeadRow.jsx: 'Save note' button only disables while note === lead.note, but after successful patch the local `note` state is not re-synced from the server response — subsequent server-side normalization (trim) would leave the button enabled with no change to save. Minor UX nit.

Admin.jsx CSV export writes a BOM + semicolons which is fine for Excel-IT but has no header row localization and includes raw ISO created_at; consider formatting dates it-IT for consistency with the UI.
Admin at 390px: KPI grid uses grid-cols-2 which forces two columns and makes the 'Conversione' KPI span a single orphan row — visually acceptable but a 1-col stacked layout on <sm would be cleaner.

rca of the issue: Admin /auth/me 403 bug: /api/auth/me endpoint was placed on `api = APIRouter(prefix='/api', dependencies=[Depends(require_role(current_user, 'doctor'))])`, which enforces doctor-only access on every route it owns. The admin cookie satisfies `current_user` (session valid) but fails `require_role('doctor')` → 403. The frontend AuthProvider (lib/auth.js:15) treats any non-2xx from api.me() as 'not authenticated', so the admin was redirected to Login after each successful login (infinite loop). Fix: moved the single-line @api.get('/auth/me') route to @public_api.get('/auth/me') — public_api has no role dependency, only the `Depends(current_user)` on the handler, which still enforces authentication. Reproduction: before fix, `curl -c jar -X POST .../api/auth/login -d admin creds` returned 200, then `curl -b jar .../api/auth/me` returned 403 'Accesso non consentito per questo account'. After fix: 200 with the admin user payload.
